chunks.content: Google announced on 2025-03-18 that it had agreed to acquire Wiz, the cloud-security firm, for approximately $32 billion in an all-cash deal — the largest acquisition in Google's history. The deal followed Wiz's rejection of Google's earlier $23 billion offer in July 2024. Wiz co-founder and CEO Assaf Rappaport remained a named principal in the transaction. Google Cloud, under Thomas Kurian, pursued Wiz to close the security gap with AWS and Azure, betting on cloud-security consolidation as the cloud wars' next battleground and on AI-driven cloud adoption as the demand driver. The deal closed in 2025 after shareholder and regulatory steps, with completion reported in July 2025.

prior_gap_texts: Google announced on March 18, 2025 that it had agreed to acquire cloud-security firm Wiz for approximately $32 billion in an all-cash deal [Source: ev-1].
This transaction represented the largest acquisition in Google's history and followed Wiz’s rejection of a previous offer from Google worth $23 billion in July 2024 [Source: ev-1].

The primary motivation for the acquisition was strategic; under Thomas Kurian, Google Cloud sought to close its security gap with competitors AWS and Azure by pursuing consolidation in the cloud-security sector [Source: ev-1].
While the deal closed after shareholder and regulatory steps were completed—reported in July 2025—the initial announcement occurred in March 2025 [Source: ev-1].
